checks: Unique support localizes the closed shallow K cap to the chosen cell. For fixed small depth the compact cap lies inside the open cell; a sequence of contrary points in the corresponding outer caps would converge into the K cap outside the cell, which is impossible.

The outer excess per cell is nonnegative and bounded by |P_j|−|K|→0 via outer parallel sets. The cap at the fixed depth has positive volume independently of j. Continuous threshold variation up to the outer support therefore removes precisely the cell excess. If the excess is zero the support threshold leaves all volume unchanged.

Removed regions are confined to separate cells and commute. The exact thresholds converge to their old supports because any fixed positive depth contains positive old volume and outer supports converge. Every fixed inner homothetic copy survives all cuts eventually; with the outer approximation this proves Hausdorff convergence and eventual positive volume, including d=1.

overlap.comparison: Its supporting-normal geometry localizes an addition near one exposed support point. It does not correct excesses of a circumscribed polytope in distinct open arrangement cells or preserve their exact volumes.

readability: The proof and its scope are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The positive shallow cap at each exposed point provides an independent exact correction in its open arrangement cell.
